messages.author: 1e58b48645aa018b
messages.subject: Saving Shinystan sessions?
parts:
Hello,

 have a large STAN model that takes several hours to open in my browser using launch_shinystan().  I was wondering if there was a way to save the “session” (for lack of a better word) in memory such that I could automatically open it from my hard drive, rather than sending everything to the Cloud again (which I assume is why I take so long).

Thanks,

John

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: Saving Shinystan sessions?
parts:
Hi John, 

I don't have a great answer, but I might have a somewhat helpful suggestion. 

First, when you call launch_shinystan it doesn't actually send anything to the cloud. Everything is happening locally on your machine and the web browser is just used to display the content. What's slow is that when you call launch_shinystan it has to do a bunch of computations before it can show you anything. Usually that doesn't take long but for very large models it can take quite some time unfortunately, as you've noticed. 

When you say you have a large model, do you mean it has a lot of parameters? That's usually the culprit when it takes so long.  If it does have a lot of parameters, do you need to look at all of them in shinystan or are you mostly interested in looking at a subset of them? If the latter, then there's a new function called drop_parameters that will be introduced in the next version of the shinystan package that might help. It's already available in the version of shinystan on the develop branch on github, which you can install using 

devtools::install_github("stan-dev/shinystan", ref = "develop")

Then you could do something like this:

sso <- as.shinystan(fit) # still could take a very long time to initially create the shinystan object
sso <- drop_parameters(sso, pars = c("alpha", "theta")) # but use the names of some parameters in your model
launch_shinystan(sso) # should be faster than launch_shinystan(fit)

If any of the parameters in pars are non-scalar (e.g. vectors, matrices, etc.) then all of their elements will be dropped. 

Creating sso will still take a long time, but then if you drop a bunch of parameters that you don't need to look at the slimmer sso should launch faster. And you can save the smaller sso so you don't need to repeat the process of creating the original sso if you want to launch shinystan again at some later time. 

Unfortunately there's not really a better option at the moment, although I'm planning on eventually modifying the as.shinystan function so it can drop parameters internally if the user specifies some parameters to remove. That would be faster than having to create sso using all parameters and then dropping them. 

Hope that helps, 

Jonah

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Saving Shinystan sessions?
parts:
A few other tips that might not be applicable in this case but might be useful for future reference:

1) If your model has a lot of parameters/transformed parameters, then if some are not of direct interest you can specify pars when calling stan() in rstan which will only save the parameters in pars and give you a smaller stanfit object and in turn a smaller shinystan object. Some transformed parameters may also be able to be declared and defined in the model block, in which case they won't be saved but you can still use them in the model. 

2) launch_shinystan will always be faster if the input is a shinystan object rather than a stanfit object. This is because it first converts the stanfit object to a shinystan object. So if you might end up calling launch_shinystan more than once it's a good idea to first create a shinystan object and use that. For small models the difference is negligible but for large models it can make a big difference.

Jonah
